fact: Newsmada reports that the UGD, with World Bank-backed Prodigy and the digital ministry, launched the first stage of Rahaka on 28 April 2026, an X-Road-based secure data exchange layer, under decree n°2025-1959 on interoperability of public information systems; it names no connected bodies or data flows yet.

Biometric Update reports that Madagascar's Digital Governance Unit (UGD), under the World Bank-financed PRODIGY project, issued a call for expressions of interest in August 2025 for a firm to help operationalise and scale up the national interoperability platform, with bidders required to have deployed X-Road or equivalent platforms.

fact: The UGD's interoperability framework (v1.0.2) states that the Orinasa project set up the first interoperable ecosystem, which allowed secure data exchange between EDBM, DGI, MINJUS and INSTAT; no date is given for the event, so the page's last-update date is used.

The World Bank blog says the Madagascar government is developing an interoperability platform based on X-Road to enable rapid and secure exchange of data between different government information systems, with the civil registration and ID databases as core layers and interoperability planned with the national social registry.

L'Express reports that the Rahaka national exchange system is already operational at five bodies, EDBM, CNaPS, Instat, the Ministry of Justice and the Direction generale des Impots, at the 28 April 2026 launch.

INSTAT says the 28 April 2026 ceremony launched national interoperability between ministries and public institutions, a shared IT system for exchanging data, and the first convention on using the RAHAKA system was signed by the UGD, several ministries and private-sector actors.

INSTAT reports the official launch on 28 April 2026 of national interoperability, a shared IT system for ministries and public bodies to exchange data, with the first RAHAKA usage convention signed by UGD, several ministries, private actors and INSTAT; it gives no count of connected systems.

The Système d'échange national (SEN), run by the Unité de gouvernance digitale, already interconnects 14 institutions and supports services including Orinasa, Lucy, Hetra Online, the RNCS and the SRNE, per the 2424.mg report of the April 2026 launch.
14 institutions are connected to the Système d'échange national, according to 2424.mg.
The Programme de réformes pour l'efficacité de l'administration (PREA) reports more than 162,000 exchanges recorded through the SEN to date.
